kurz: A wafer-thin layer of cornflour on dry potatoes or poultry skin turns into a fine, crisp shell in the oven.
bild_im_kopf: Like powder on damp skin: it takes up the last moisture and forms its own dry layer.
was_passiert: The [[staerke|starch]] takes up the remaining surface moisture and swells a little there. In the hot oven this thin layer dries out and hardens into a brittle shell.
warum_wichtig: A simple route to more crispness when soaking or parboiling is too much effort.
faustregeln: A dusting, not a layer: too much starch turns floury and powdery.
schritte: Dust lightly with cornflour in a bowl and toss.
Tap off the excess: it should be just a hint.
Toss with a little oil and bake hot.
